10	/-!
11	# B3 — the fibre chart comparison: `hfib` from fibrewise `h¹`-vanishing
12	
13	The frozen wave-4 ℙ¹ engine
14	`AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.p1Cech_h0_baseChange_of_fibrewise_h1_vanishing`
15	(`Picard/RigidPushforwardP1Engine.lean` §5) consumes a hypothesis `hfib`
16	phrased *algebraically*: for every maximal ideal `𝔪` of the base ring
17	`R₀ = Γ(Spec A, ⊤)` the base-changed Čech difference map
18	`d ⊗_{R₀} (R₀ ⧸ 𝔪)` is surjective, where `d` is the two-term Čech complex
19	of the standard 2-chart cover `𝒰 = p1BaseChangeCoverSquare A` of `ℙ¹_A`.
20	
21	The *geometric* input available on the campaign is instead the fibrewise
22	Čech `h¹`-vanishing `Scheme.Hom.FiberH1Vanishing` on the scheme-theoretic
23	fibres `ℙ¹_t = p⁻¹(t)`.  Bridging the two is the classical "cohomology and
24	base change" chart computation (Mumford, *Abelian Varieties* II §5; EGA III
25	7.7; Stacks 02KG at `i = 0`): the section ring square of the cartesian
26	fibre square is a **pushout**, so the Čech complex of the fibre cover is the
27	scalar extension of the Čech complex of `𝒰` along `R₀ → κ(t)`.
28	
29	This file builds that bridge in the following layers.
30	
31	* **§1 (Brick 1).**  `isPushout_appLE_of_isPullback'` — the section-ring
32	  pushout of a cartesian square on *arbitrary* compatible affine opens.
33	  The pre-existing `isPushout_appLE_of_isPullback`
34	  (`Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer.lean`) is pinned to the open `f ⁻¹ᵁ V`,
35	  which for the projection `p : ℙ¹_A ⟶ Spec A` and `V = ⊤` is all of `ℙ¹_A`
36	  and hence *not affine*; the generalisation below takes any affine
37	  `U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V`, which is what the chart-by-chart computation needs.
38	
39	* **§2 (Brick 2).**  `Scheme.Hom.isPullback_fiberι` — the fibre square
40	  `X_t → X`, `X_t → Spec κ(t)`, `f`, `fromSpecResidueField t` is cartesian
41	  (it *is* the defining pullback of `Scheme.Hom.fiber`).
42	
43	* **§3 (Brick 3).**  `isPushout_appLE_fiberChart` — combining §1 and §2 at
44	  `V = O = ⊤`: for an affine open `W ⊆ X` of the total space of a family
45	  `f : X ⟶ Y` over an affine base,
46	  `Γ(X_t, W_t) = Γ(X, W) ⊗_{Γ(Y, ⊤)} Γ(Spec κ(t), ⊤)`.
47	
48	* **§4.**  `pullback_app_isoTensor_baseMap_res'` — a public re-derivation of
49	  the `private` QuotScheme lemma saying that the canonical base map commutes
50	  with restriction.
51	
52	* **§5 (Brick 4).**  `exists_fiberChartTensorEquiv` — the chart fibre
53	  comparison `Θ_W : Γ(Spec κ(t), ⊤) ⊗_{Γ(Y, ⊤)} Γ(M, W) ≃+ Γ(M_t, W_t)`,
54	  assembled from the affine section formula of `Picard/QuotScheme.lean` and
55	  the associativity bridge of `Picard/SectionBaseChange.lean` along the §3
56	  pushout.
57	
58	* **§6 (Brick 5).**  `fiberChart_smul_baseMap_res` — the comparisons `Θ_W`
59	  are natural in `W`, so they form a map of Čech complexes.
60	
61	* **§7 (Brick 6).**
62	  `Scheme.AffineCoverMVSquare.surjective_moduleSectionDiffBase_baseChange_residueField`
63	  — the headline geometric statement: for a family over an affine base and a
64	  2-affine cover, fibrewise Čech `h¹`-vanishing at `t` implies surjectivity
65	  of the `κ(t)`-base change of the Čech difference map.
66	
67	* **§8 (Brick 8).**  `surjective_baseChange_of_algEquiv` — base-changed
68	  surjectivity only depends on the isomorphism class of the scalar algebra.
69	
70	* **§9 (Brick 7).**  `exists_point_appLE_fromSpecResidueField_of_isMaximal` —
71	  every maximal ideal of `Γ(Spec R, ⊤)` is the kernel of a (surjective)
72	  residue-field evaluation, so `Γ(Spec R, ⊤) ⧸ 𝔪 ≅ Γ(Spec κ(t), ⊤)`.
73	
74	* **§10.**  `Adelic.p1_hfib_of_fiberH1Vanishing` — the consumer form: the
75	  hypothesis `_hfib` of the wave-4 ℙ¹ engine, verbatim, deduced from
76	  fibrewise `h¹`-vanishing on the fibres of `ℙ¹_A ⟶ Spec A`.
77	
78	Source: Stacks 02KG / 01HQ; Mumford, *Abelian Varieties* II §5;
79	EGA III 7.7.5.
80	-/

90	/-! ## §1 (Brick 1). The section-ring pushout on arbitrary affine opens -/
91	
92	section SectionRingPushoutGeneral
93	
94	variable {Y Y' X X' : Scheme.{u}}
95	
96	/-- **The section-ring square of a cartesian square is a pushout, on
97	arbitrary compatible affine opens.**
98	
99	For a cartesian square
100	
101	```
102	  X' --g'--> X
103	  |f'        |f
104	  v          v
105	  Y' --g---> Y
106	```
107	
108	affine opens `V ⊆ Y`, `O ⊆ Y'`, `U ⊆ X` with `O ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ V`, `U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V`,
109	and `U' = g' ⁻¹ᵁ U ⊓ f' ⁻¹ᵁ O`, the induced square of section rings
110	
111	```
112	  Γ(Y, V) ----> Γ(X, U)
113	     |             |
114	     v             v
115	  Γ(Y', O) ---> Γ(X', U')
116	```
117	
118	is a pushout in `CommRingCat`, i.e. `Γ(X', U') = Γ(X, U) ⊗_{Γ(Y, V)} Γ(Y', O)`
119	(Stacks 01HQ / EGA I 3.2.5 in the affine-chart form).  Affineness of `U'` is
120	*not* a hypothesis: the restricted square `U' → U`, `U' → O`, `U → V`,
121	`O → V` is cartesian (`Scheme.Hom.isPullback_resLE`), so `U'` is a fibre
122	product of affine schemes and hence affine, and Mathlib's
123	`isPushout_appTop_of_isPullback` applies; the resulting pushout of `appTop`s
124	is transported to the `appLE` maps along the four `Scheme.Opens.topIso`s
125	(`Scheme.Hom.resLE_app_top`).
126	
127	This is the `U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V` generalisation of
128	`AlgebraicGeometry.isPushout_appLE_of_isPullback`
129	(`Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer.lean`), which is pinned to `U = f ⁻¹ᵁ V`.
130	The generalisation is what the ℙ¹ fibre-chart computation needs: there
131	`f = p : ℙ¹_A ⟶ Spec A`, `V = ⊤`, and `f ⁻¹ᵁ V = ℙ¹_A` is not affine, while
132	the individual charts of the standard 2-chart cover are. -/
133	theorem isPushout_appLE_of_isPullback'
134	    {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {g' : X' ⟶ X}
135	    (h : IsPullback g' f' f g)
136	    {V : Y.Opens} {O : Y'.Opens} {U : X.Opens} {U' : X'.Opens}
137	    (eO : O ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ V) (eU : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V)
138	    (hU'eq : U' = g' ⁻¹ᵁ U ⊓ f' ⁻¹ᵁ O)
139	    (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (hO : IsAffineOpen O) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) :
140	    CategoryTheory.IsPushout (f.appLE V U eU) (g.appLE V O eO)
141	      (g'.appLE U U' (hU'eq.le.trans inf_le_left))
142	      (f'.appLE O U' (hU'eq.le.trans inf_le_right)) := by
143	  have hpb := Scheme.Hom.isPullback_resLE h (US := V) (UT := O) (UX := U) eO eU hU'eq
144	  haveI : IsAffine V.toScheme := hV
145	  haveI : IsAffine O.toScheme := hO
146	  haveI : IsAffine U.toScheme := hU
147	  have hpush := isPushout_appTop_of_isPullback hpb
148	  have key : ∀ {A B : Scheme.{u}} (φ : A ⟶ B) (W₀ : B.Opens) (W : A.Opens)
149	      (ew : W ≤ φ ⁻¹ᵁ W₀),
150	      (φ.resLE W₀ W ew).appTop ≫ W.topIso.hom = W₀.topIso.hom ≫ φ.appLE W₀ W ew := by
151	    intro A B φ W₀ W ew
152	    rw [show (φ.resLE W₀ W ew).appTop = (φ.resLE W₀ W ew).app ⊤ from rfl,
153	      Scheme.Hom.resLE_app_top]
154	    simp only [Category.assoc, Iso.inv_hom_id, Category.comp_id]
155	  exact hpush.of_iso (Scheme.Opens.topIso V) (Scheme.Opens.topIso U)
156	    (Scheme.Opens.topIso O) (Scheme.Opens.topIso U')
157	    (key f V U eU) (key g V O eO)
158	    (key g' U U' (hU'eq.le.trans inf_le_left))
159	    (key f' O U' (hU'eq.le.trans inf_le_right))
160	
161	end SectionRingPushoutGeneral
162	
163	/-! ## §2 (Brick 2). The fibre square is cartesian -/
164	
165	section FiberSquare
166	
167	variable {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
168	
169	/-- **The scheme-theoretic fibre square is cartesian.**  By definition
170	`f.fiber t = pullback f (Y.fromSpecResidueField t)` with `f.fiberι t` the
171	first and `f.fiberToSpecResidueField t` the second projection, so the square
172	
173	```
174	  X_t --fiberι--> X
175	   |               |f
176	   v               v
177	 Spec κ(t) -----> Y
178	```
179	
180	is the defining cartesian square (Stacks 01JW). -/
181	theorem Scheme.Hom.isPullback_fiberι (f : X ⟶ Y) (t : Y) :
182	    IsPullback (f.fiberι t) (f.fiberToSpecResidueField t) f
183	      (Y.fromSpecResidueField t) :=
184	  IsPullback.of_hasPullback _ _
185	
186	end FiberSquare
187	
188	/-! ## §3 (Brick 3). The chart-level pushout at a fibre -/
189	
190	section FiberChartPushout
191	
192	variable {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
193	
194	/-- **The fibre chart section-ring pushout.**  For a family `f : X ⟶ Y` over
195	an *affine* base `Y`, a point `t : Y` and an affine open `W ⊆ X`, the square
196	
197	```
198	  Γ(Y, ⊤) --------> Γ(X, W)
199	     |                 |
200	     v                 v
201	  Γ(Spec κ(t), ⊤) -> Γ(X_t, fiberι ⁻¹ᵁ W)
202	```
203	
204	is a pushout of commutative rings.  Brick 1 applied to the cartesian fibre
205	square of Brick 2 at `V = O = ⊤`, `U = W`,
206	`U' = f.fiberι t ⁻¹ᵁ W = (f.fiberι t ⁻¹ᵁ W) ⊓ (f.fiberToSpecResidueField t ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤)`.
207	
208	Geometrically: the chart of the fibre over `t` cut out by `W` is the base
209	change of the chart `W` along `Spec κ(t) → Y` (Stacks 01HQ). -/
210	theorem isPushout_appLE_fiberChart (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffine Y] (t : Y)
211	    {W : X.Opens} (hW : IsAffineOpen W) :
212	    CategoryTheory.IsPushout
213	      (f.appLE ⊤ W le_top)
214	      ((Y.fromSpecResidueField t).appLE ⊤ ⊤ le_top)
215	      ((f.fiberι t).appLE W (f.fiberι t ⁻¹ᵁ W) le_rfl)
216	      ((f.fiberToSpecResidueField t).appLE ⊤ (f.fiberι t ⁻¹ᵁ W) le_top) :=
217	  isPushout_appLE_of_isPullback' (f.isPullback_fiberι t) le_top le_top
218	    (inf_top_eq _).symm (isAffineOpen_top Y) (isAffineOpen_top _) hW
219	
220	end FiberChartPushout

222	/-! ## §4 (Brick 5, core). Restriction naturality of the canonical base map -/
223	
224	section BaseMapRes
225	
226	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
227	/-- **The canonical base map commutes with restriction.**  For `g : Y ⟶ X`,
228	a module `N` on `X`, opens `V'' ≤ V'` of `X` and `W'' ≤ W'` of `Y` with
229	`W' ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ V'` and `W'' ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ V''`, restricting the canonical base-map
230	image `Γ(N, V') → Γ(g^* N, W')` to `W''` equals the base-map image of the
231	restriction of the section to `V''`:
232	
233	`(g^* N)(W'' ← W') ∘ baseMap = baseMap ∘ N(V'' ← V')`.
234	
235	Naturality of the `pullback ⊣ pushforward` adjunction unit in the open,
236	followed by collapse of the two composite restrictions
237	(`Scheme.Modules.sections_map_map`).
238	
239	This is a **public** re-derivation of the `private` QuotScheme lemma
240	`pullback_app_isoTensor_baseMap_res` (`Picard/QuotScheme.lean` §02KE step
241	(6)); the precedent for such a re-derivation is
242	`AlgebraicGeometry.pullback_map_app_isoTensor_baseMap`
243	(`Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer.lean`), which likewise replaces the
244	private restriction-collapse lemma `modules_res_res_hom` by the public
245	`Scheme.Modules.sections_map_map`. -/
246	lemma pullback_app_isoTensor_baseMap_res' {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ X)
247	    (N : X.Modules) {V' V'' : X.Opens} {W' W'' : Y.Opens}
248	    (hW' : W' ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ V') (hW'' : W'' ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ V'')
249	    (hV : V'' ≤ V') (hW : W'' ≤ W') (x : Γ(N, V')) :
250	    (((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj N).presheaf.map (homOfLE hW).op).hom
251	        (pullback_app_isoTensor_baseMap g N hW' x)
252	      = pullback_app_isoTensor_baseMap g N hW''
253	        ((N.presheaf.map (homOfLE hV).op).hom x) := by
254	  have hnat := congrArg
255	    (fun (k : Γ(N, V') ⟶
256	        Γ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward g).obj ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj N), V'')) =>
257	      (AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom k) x)
258	    ((Scheme.Modules.Hom.mapPresheaf
259	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction g).unit.app N)).naturality
260	      (homOfLE hV).op)
261	  have hL := Scheme.Modules.sections_map_map ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj N)
262	    (homOfLE hW) (homOfLE hW') (homOfLE (hW.trans hW'))
263	    ((Scheme.Modules.Hom.app
264	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction g).unit.app N) V').hom x)
265	  have hR := Scheme.Modules.sections_map_map ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj N)
266	    (homOfLE hW'') ((Opens.map g.base).map (homOfLE hV)) (homOfLE (hW.trans hW'))
267	    ((Scheme.Modules.Hom.app
268	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction g).unit.app N) V').hom x)
269	  change (((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj N).presheaf.map (homOfLE hW).op).hom
270	      ((((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj N).presheaf.map (homOfLE hW').op).hom
271	        ((Scheme.Modules.Hom.app
272	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction g).unit.app N) V').hom x))
273	    = (((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj N).presheaf.map (homOfLE hW'').op).hom
274	        ((Scheme.Modules.Hom.app
275	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction g).unit.app N) V'').hom
276	          ((N.presheaf.map (homOfLE hV).op).hom x))
277	  rw [hL]
278	  refine hR.symm.trans ?_
279	  exact (congrArg
280	    (fun w => (((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj N).presheaf.map (homOfLE hW'').op).hom w)
281	    hnat).symm
282	
283	end BaseMapRes

285	/-! ## §5 (Brick 4). The chart fibre comparison `Θ_W` -/
286	
287	section FiberChartComparison
288	
289	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
290	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
291	-- Heartbeat headroom for the five-algebra `letI` dictionary of the fibre-chart
292	-- square and the section-formula transports, as in the Lane-F layer of
293	-- `Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer.lean`.
294	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 800000 in
295	/-- **The chart fibre comparison isomorphism** (Stacks 02KG at `i = 0`, chart
296	form; Mumford AV II §5).  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a family over an affine base,
297	`M` a quasi-coherent module on `X`, `t : Y` a point and `W ⊆ X` an affine
298	open whose fibre chart `W_t = f.fiberι t ⁻¹ᵁ W` is again affine.  Then the
299	sections of the fibre restriction `M_t` over `W_t` are the scalar extension
300	of `Γ(M, W)` along `Γ(Y, ⊤) → κ(t)`:
301	
302	`Γ(Spec κ(t), ⊤) ⊗_{Γ(Y, ⊤)} Γ(M, W) ≅ Γ(M_t, W_t)`,
303	
304	as additive groups, the isomorphism sending `b ⊗ x` to
305	`b · (canonical base-map image of x)`.
306	
307	The proof composes two existing pieces:
308	
309	* the **affine section formula**
310	  `pullback_app_isoTensor_baseMap_sectionLinearEquiv` (`Picard/QuotScheme.lean`,
311	  Stacks 01HQ) applied to the fibre embedding, giving
312	  `Γ(X_t, W_t) ⊗_{Γ(X, W)} Γ(M, W) ≅ Γ(M_t, W_t)`;
313	* the **associativity bridge** `SectionBaseChange.bijective_addHom_of_isPushout`
314	  (`Picard/SectionBaseChange.lean`) along the fibre-chart section-ring pushout
315	  of Brick 3 (`isPushout_appLE_fiberChart`), which rewrites the tensor factor
316	  `Γ(X_t, W_t) = Γ(X, W) ⊗_{Γ(Y, ⊤)} Γ(Spec κ(t), ⊤)` and cancels.
317	
318	Only additivity is asserted: the source is a `Γ(Spec κ(t), ⊤)`-module and the
319	target a `Γ(X_t, W_t)`-module, and the comparison is semilinear over the
320	structural map between them — which is exactly the content of the displayed
321	formula for `Θ (b ⊗ₜ x)`.
322	
323	The assembly mirrors `isIso_pushforwardBaseChangeMap_app_of_isPullback`
324	(`Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer.lean`), which performs the same two-step
325	identification for the pushforward base-change mate. -/
326	theorem exists_fiberChartTensorEquiv {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffine Y] (t : Y)
327	    (M : X.Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent] {W : X.Opens} (hW : IsAffineOpen W)
328	    (hWt : IsAffineOpen (f.fiberι t ⁻¹ᵁ W)) :
329	    letI : Algebra Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(Spec (Y.residueField t), ⊤) :=
330	      ((Y.fromSpecResidueField t).appLE ⊤ ⊤ le_top).hom.toAlgebra
331	    letI := f.baseSectionsModule M W
332	    Nonempty { Θ : TensorProduct Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(Spec (Y.residueField t), ⊤) Γ(M, W) ≃+
333	        Γ(f.fiberModule t M, f.fiberι t ⁻¹ᵁ W) //
334	      ∀ (b : Γ(Spec (Y.residueField t), ⊤)) (x : Γ(M, W)),
335	        Θ (b ⊗ₜ[Γ(Y, ⊤)] x) =
336	          ((f.fiberToSpecResidueField t).appLE ⊤ (f.fiberι t ⁻¹ᵁ W) le_top).hom b •
337	            pullback_app_isoTensor_baseMap (f.fiberι t) M
338	              (le_refl (f.fiberι t ⁻¹ᵁ W)) x } := by
339	  letI aAB : Algebra Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(Spec (Y.residueField t), ⊤) :=
340	    ((Y.fromSpecResidueField t).appLE ⊤ ⊤ le_top).hom.toAlgebra
341	  letI mAM := f.baseSectionsModule M W
342	  -- the algebra dictionary of the fibre-chart section-ring square
343	  letI aAC : Algebra Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(X, W) := (f.appLE ⊤ W le_top).hom.toAlgebra
344	  letI aCD : Algebra Γ(X, W) Γ(f.fiber t, f.fiberι t ⁻¹ᵁ W) :=
345	    ((f.fiberι t).appLE W (f.fiberι t ⁻¹ᵁ W) le_rfl).hom.toAlgebra
346	  letI aBD : Algebra Γ(Spec (Y.residueField t), ⊤) Γ(f.fiber t, f.fiberι t ⁻¹ᵁ W) :=
347	    ((f.fiberToSpecResidueField t).appLE ⊤ (f.fiberι t ⁻¹ᵁ W) le_top).hom.toAlgebra
348	  letI aAD : Algebra Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(f.fiber t, f.fiberι t ⁻¹ᵁ W) :=
349	    ((f.appLE ⊤ W le_top) ≫
350	      ((f.fiberι t).appLE W (f.fiberι t ⁻¹ᵁ W) le_rfl)).hom.toAlgebra
351	  have hsq := (isPushout_appLE_fiberChart f t hW).w
352	  haveI tACD : IsScalarTower Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(X, W) Γ(f.fiber t, f.fiberι t ⁻¹ᵁ W) :=
353	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq (fun _ => rfl)
354	  haveI tABD : IsScalarTower Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(Spec (Y.residueField t), ⊤)
355	      Γ(f.fiber t, f.fiberι t ⁻¹ᵁ W) :=
356	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq (fun r => by
357	      have h0 := congrArg
358	        (fun (φ : Γ(Y, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(f.fiber t, f.fiberι t ⁻¹ᵁ W)) => φ.hom r) hsq
359	      simp only [CommRingCat.hom_comp, RingHom.comp_apply] at h0
360	      exact h0)
361	  haveI pushAlg : Algebra.IsPushout Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(X, W) Γ(Spec (Y.residueField t), ⊤)
362	      Γ(f.fiber t, f.fiberι t ⁻¹ᵁ W) :=
363	    (CommRingCat.isPushout_iff_isPushout).mp (isPushout_appLE_fiberChart f t hW)
364	  haveI tACM : IsScalarTower Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(X, W) Γ(M, W) :=
365	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_smul (fun _ _ => rfl)
366	  -- the affine section formula for the fibre embedding
367	  obtain ⟨⟨eL, heL⟩⟩ :=
368	    pullback_app_isoTensor_baseMap_sectionLinearEquiv (f.fiberι t) M hWt hW
369	      (le_refl (f.fiberι t ⁻¹ᵁ W))
370	  -- the scalar-extension bridge along the fibre-chart pushout

484	2-affine cover of `X`, `M` a quasi-coherent module on `X`, and `t : Y` a

486	(`Scheme.Hom.FiberH1Vanishing`).  Then the `κ(t)`-base change of the
487	`Γ(Y, ⊤)`-linear Čech difference map
488	`d : Γ(M, U₁) × Γ(M, U₂) → Γ(M, U₁ ⊓ U₂)` is surjective.

492	
493	```
494	  κ(t) ⊗ (Γ(M,U₁) × Γ(M,U₂)) --d ⊗ κ(t)--> κ(t) ⊗ Γ(M, U₁ ⊓ U₂)

496	      v                                          v

501	naturality of Brick 5, and whose three vertical maps are bijections.  The

504	fibrewise vanishing transfers to the specific preimage cover

506	(`Scheme.Hom.FiberH1Vanishing.surjective_moduleSectionDiff`).  Surjectivity

511	    (h1 : f.FiberH1Vanishing M t) :
512	    letI : Algebra Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(Spec (Y.residueField t), ⊤) :=

514	    letI := f.baseSectionsModule M 𝒰.U₁
515	    letI := f.baseSectionsModule M 𝒰.U₂
516	    letI := f.baseSectionsModule M (𝒰.U₁ ⊓ 𝒰.U₂)

518	      Γ(Spec (Y.residueField t), ⊤)) := by
519	  letI aAB : Algebra Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(Spec (Y.residueField t), ⊤) :=
520	    ((Y.fromSpecResidueField t).appLE ⊤ ⊤ le_top).hom.toAlgebra

522	  letI mA2 := f.baseSectionsModule M 𝒰.U₂

527	    (𝒰.isAffineOpen_U₂.preimage (f.fiberι t))

531	    Scheme.Hom.fiberModule_isQuasicoherent f t M

533	      ⇑((𝒰.preimage (f.fiberι t)).moduleSectionDiff (f.fiberModule t M)) :=
534	    h1.surjective_moduleSectionDiff (𝒰.preimage (f.fiberι t))
535	  -- the commuting Čech square, checked on pure tensors
536	  have hsquare : ∀ w : TensorProduct Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(Spec (Y.residueField t), ⊤)
537	      (Γ(M, 𝒰.U₁) × Γ(M, 𝒰.U₂)),
538	      Θ₀ ((𝒰.moduleSectionDiffBase f M).baseChange
539	          Γ(Spec (Y.residueField t), ⊤) w) =
540	        (𝒰.preimage (f.fiberι t)).moduleSectionDiff (f.fiberModule t M)

570	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := hdt (Θ₀ z)

630	`ε⁻¹(m) ⊆ R` obtained by transporting `m` across the canonical
631	`ε : Γ(Spec R, ⊤) ≃+* R` (`Scheme.ΓSpecIso`), and the structural map
632	factors as
633	
634	`Γ(Spec R, ⊤) --ε--> R --algebraMap--> κ(t.asIdeal) --≅--> Γ(Spec κ(t), ⊤)`
635

638	`Ideal.algebraMap_residueField_surjective` (valid because `t.asIdeal` is

643	    ∃ t : Spec R,
644	      Function.Surjective
645	          ⇑(((Spec R).fromSpecResidueField t).appLE ⊤ ⊤ le_top).hom ∧
646	        RingHom.ker (((Spec R).fromSpecResidueField t).appLE ⊤ ⊤ le_top).hom = m := by
647	  letI := hm
648	  let ε : Γ(Spec R, ⊤) ≃+* R := (Scheme.ΓSpecIso R).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv

650	    Ideal.comap_isMaximal_of_surjective _ ε.symm.surjective
651	  set t : Spec R :=
652	    ⟨Ideal.comap (ε.symm : R →+* Γ(Spec R, ⊤)) m, hmax.isPrime⟩ with ht
653	  -- the residue-field comparison, as a ring isomorphism onto the section ring

655	      Γ(Spec ((Spec R).residueField t), ⊤) :=

657	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso ((Spec R).residueField t)).symm

667	        (Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso R t).inv ≫
668	        (Scheme.ΓSpecIso ((Spec R).residueField t)).inv := by
669	    rw [← Scheme.Spec.map_residueFieldIso_inv_eq_fromSpecResidueField R t,
670	      Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop, hnat, hnat]
671	    simp only [Category.assoc, Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc]
672	    rfl
673	  have happ : ∀ x : Γ(Spec R, ⊤),
674	      (((Spec R).fromSpecResidueField t).appLE ⊤ ⊤ le_top).hom x =

676	          (algebraMap R t.asIdeal.ResidueField (ε x)) := by

/-!
# Affine-target descent for the pushforward base-change mate

The B3 campaign gate `Scheme.HasRigidPushforward` (`Picard/RigidPushforward.lean`:373) has two
fields.  `Picard/RigidPushforwardGate.lean` ("Caveat on the `baseChange` field") and
`Picard/RigidPushforwardFrontier.lean` (item 3 of "What remains") both record that the second
one, `Scheme.RigidPushforwardBaseChange` (`Picard/RigidPushforward.lean`:342), has **no
infrastructure at all**: every `IsIso` theorem for the adjoint mate `pushforwardBaseChangeMap`
in this tree (`isIso_pushforwardBaseChangeMap_of_isPullback`,
`Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer.lean`:1108, and its chart form :949) assumes `[IsAffineHom f]`,
whereas the gate's family `q : C_A ⟶ Spec A` is proper and emphatically not affine.

This file replaces "no infrastructure" by a named, honest **reduction**: the whole field follows
from a single classical `H⁰`-base-change bijectivity of `Γ(Spec A, ⊤)`-modules.  It does *not*
prove that bijectivity — see "What remains" below — and it does not smuggle in the non-affine
case: only the two *bases* of the square are assumed affine, the fibre map `f` is arbitrary.

## The reduction, in four steps

* **§1 — affine-target descent.**  `Scheme.Modules.isIso_of_isIso_moduleSpecΓFunctor_map` and
  `Scheme.Modules.isIso_of_bijective_appTop`: a morphism `φ : M ⟶ N` of quasi-coherent modules
  on an affine scheme is an isomorphism as soon as it is *bijective on global sections*.  The
  input is the affine structure theorem `Scheme.Modules.isIso_fromTildeΓ_of_isQuasicoherent`
  (Stacks 01I8, `Picard/QuotScheme.lean`:2693) — the counit `Γ(M, ⊤)~ ⟶ M` is an isomorphism
  for quasi-coherent `M` — together with naturality of `Scheme.Modules.fromTildeΓNatTrans`.
  Naturality rewrites `φ` as `fromTildeΓ_M⁻¹ ≫ (Γφ)~ ≫ fromTildeΓ_N`, a composite of three
  isomorphisms, and the resulting `Iso` has `φ` as its `hom` by `rfl`.

* **§2 — the mate on global sections.**  `isIso_pushforwardBaseChangeMap_appTop_of_bijective`:
  over affine bases the `Γ(⊤)`-component of `pushforwardBaseChangeMap` *is* the canonical map
  `Γ(Y', ⊤) ⊗_{Γ(Y, ⊤)} Γ(f_* F, ⊤) → Γ(f'_* (g'^* F), ⊤)`, `b ⊗ x ↦ b · baseMap x`.  The
  source side is identified with the tensor product by
  `pullback_app_isoTensor_baseMap_sectionLinearEquiv` (`Picard/QuotScheme.lean`:4611) and the
  formula for the mate on the image of `baseMap` is `pushforwardBaseChangeMap_app_baseMap`
  (`Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer.lean`:828) taken at `V = O = ⊤`; simple tensors are handled
  by `b ⊗ x = b • (1 ⊗ x)` and `Scheme.Modules.Hom.app_smul`, and `TensorProduct.induction_on`
  propagates.

  **Caveat, stated once and meant.**  §2 and §3 assume only `comm : g' ≫ f = f' ≫ g`; the square
  is *not* assumed cartesian.  They are therefore exactly as strong as the bijectivity `hbij`
  handed to them, and must **not** be read as an unconditional Beck–Chevalley/base-change
  theorem: all the mathematical content of a base-change theorem still sits inside `hbij`, and
  without a cartesian square there is no reason for `hbij` to hold at all.

* **§3 — the two combined.**  `isIso_pushforwardBaseChangeMap_of_bijective_gamma`: with `Y`
  affine and the target of `g` of the form `Spec R'`, quasi-coherence of both mate ends is
  automatic (`pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom`, `Scheme.Modules.pushforward_isQuasicoherent`), so
  §1 upgrades the `Γ(⊤)`-bijectivity of §2 to `IsIso` of the mate itself.  **`f` is still not
  assumed affine** — this is precisely the case the two frontier docstrings report as missing.

* **§4 — the gate's field.**  `Adelic.RigidPushforwardGammaBaseChange` names the residual
  `Γ`-level statement for the constant curve `C_A`, and
  `Adelic.rigidPushforwardBaseChange_of_gamma` derives `Scheme.RigidPushforwardBaseChange C A`

  `MorphismProperty.pullback_snd`, to know that the two pullback families are proper (hence qcqs)

## What remains, and the route the probe identified for it
